answer.content: {"sections": [{"spans": [{"text": "How many lines of code are you ", "modifiers": {}}, {"text": "reading", "modifiers": {"italic": true}}, {"text": "?", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Grab a python module\u2014something small and simple. Walk through the source until you can write down the specification of what this module does. Then put the source code away and reimplement it on your own.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Is your reimplementation faster? Slower? Why? Does your implementation pass the integration tests used by the original module? Which implementation uses more lines of code? Which has the better layout?", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Repeat the process a couple of times for larger and larger modules. You don\u2019t necessarily need to reinvent everything\u2014a single function will do if it\u2019s complicated enough.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "You\u2019ll gradually learn how to orient yourself in a large codebase: how scope is handled, how the build and test process works, the coding conventions, etc. You\u2019ll also learn a bunch of interesting corners of python that you didn\u2019t know existed.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Once you\u2019re able to read code in large projects, it\u2019ll be a lot easier to write lots of code without becoming overwhelmed.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}]}
